spec: Vague intent becomes one baselined contract. The contract gets one approval at kickoff. Execution is autonomous, milestone by milestone. Each milestone merges into dev at a checkpoint. design.high: A schema 3 contract record replaces the v1 single-PR flow and the v2 shadow flow. It binds the kickoff approval to a digest of the baseline, tracks items, milestones and reviews, merges milestones into dev with no owner dialog, and writes checkpoint and close-out reports.
design.low: lib/contract.ts holds the schema, digest and replayed reducer; lib/github.ts the readiness preflight and milestone merges; lib/brief.ts the kickoff and effect dialogs; lib/report.ts the reports; index.ts the tools, hooks and the reopen command.

defense: Approval is valid only for the digest it was given on. Nothing merges into dev without both reviews and evidence bound to the exact candidate and the required checks green. The plugin never records a human answer that an agent supplied. Every stop names one of the five reasons. A cap ends in a recorded fixed, replanned or filed disposition. There is one steering owner.

brief.markdown:
---
decision: Approve the mission contract, so missions ask you at kickoff and then stop only for the reasons in this brief.
yes: The agent builds it in three milestones. Each merges into dev after its tests and two fresh reviews pass. You get short reports, then the result is published to your Amp.
no: Nothing changes. Missions keep asking you at merges, review limits and budget limits.
risks:
  - Milestones merge into dev without your approval, however risky, once tests and two fresh reviews pass.
  - At a review limit the agent fixes, splits or files the problem itself.
  - Old mission flows and budget rules are removed, also from your published plugin.
  - Missions have no spending limit; reports show usage.
  - A wrong rule, such as a missing stop, could reach your Amp before your end review.
excluded:
  - Release to production through rolling or main, which waits until all waves are done.
  - Removing the stakeholder sign-off steps of planning and blueprinting missions.
---

## You are deciding

Approve one contract for this mission. It changes your mission skills and plugin, the tools that run your missions. Afterwards, a mission asks you once, at kickoff, and then runs on its own. Your last three missions stopped for you again and again: for merges, review limits, budgets and live checks. This is the only planned stop in this mission.

To approve, reply in the mission thread with "Approve the mission contract". You can change any of the defaults below in the same reply.

### Defaults you accept by approving

- Finished milestones merge into dev without asking you, however risky the change.
- When reviews keep failing, the agent fixes, splits or files the problem itself. A milestone merges only when no serious problem inside the checks this contract sets is open. Problems outside those checks become later work and appear in the report.
- Big work items run in child threads, and small ones as helper agents inside the mission thread.
- This mission is the first one run under the new contract.
- The old mission flows, the merge approval and all budget rules are removed, also from your published plugin.
- Publishing updates the seven skills and the plugin you already published. It adds nothing new.

### When a mission will still stop and ask you

1. Something you approved turns out to be wrong or in conflict.
2. It needs an outside action you did not approve in advance, such as a release.
3. It needs a fact only a person knows, and there is no safe default.
4. It meets a security, legal or safety line.
5. A milestone cannot be finished, even after the work was re-planned.

Planning and blueprinting missions still stop for their stakeholder sign-offs, as today.

## If you say yes

- The agent changes the skills first, so the next missions can build on them. Then it changes the plugin, then the guides.
- Each of these three milestones merges into dev when its tests and two fresh reviews pass.
- After each merge you get a short report. It asks nothing.
- At the end, the agent publishes the changed skills and plugin to your Amp. You said this needs no further approval. To withdraw that, add "ask me before publishing" to your reply.
- Publishing to your Amp at the end is not held. You confirmed that only releases to rolling and main wait for all waves.
- You then review the result when it suits you.

**What it costs you:** this approval, three short reports to read, and an end review. Agent usage is billed to your Amp account as usual, with no limit, as you asked. We cannot estimate the money in advance; each report shows the usage so far. This also applies to later missions. Our guess, not a measure, is one to three days of agent work.

## If you say no

Nothing changes. Missions keep stopping for merge approvals, review limits and budget limits. You can change a default in your reply instead of saying no.

## What changes

1. Future missions ask you once, at kickoff, in one dialog with a box to tick for each default. This mission uses your reply instead, because it builds that dialog.
2. Work is split into small items and milestones. Each milestone merges into dev, and you get a report.
3. The agent stops only for the five reasons above, or a stakeholder sign-off.
4. Budgets, the merge approval and the review-limit question are gone.
5. Before kickoff, the agent checks that GitHub, the automatic tests and every place the work will go are ready. Live checks run as scripted tests, and you get a script to try yourself.
6. The mission thread restarts child threads that stop, so none waits idle.

## What done looks like

1. A test mission with two milestones opens exactly one dialog and merges twice.
2. No skill or plugin text asks for a budget or a merge approval in dev.
3. A fresh agent, given 16 past situations, asks you only at kickoff and in the one conflict with something you approved.
4. Your published copies match the merged work, and the report names the commits.

## What we checked and what we did not

**Checked:** GitHub access, the protected dev branch, the automatic tests and both of your publishing repositories are ready. Your published copies match today's dev exactly. Fresh reviewers checked the contract and this brief three times. We fixed what they found; the last fixes were not checked again. A fourth reviewer checked the new milestone order.

**Not checked:** how the new dialog looks inside Amp itself. The mockups show it. After the second report, reply "show me the preview" to see the real dialog. The preview records nothing.

## Risks you accept

- Milestones merge into dev without your approval, however risky, once tests and two fresh reviews pass.
- At a review limit the agent fixes, splits or files the problem itself.
- Old mission flows and budget rules are removed, also from your published plugin.
- Missions have no spending limit; reports show usage.
- A wrong rule, such as a missing stop, could reach your Amp before your end review.

## Not included

- Release to production through rolling or main, which waits until all waves are done.
- Removing the stakeholder sign-off steps of planning and blueprinting missions.

## How to undo it

Reply in the mission thread at any time. Say "revert milestone 2", for example, and the agent reverts that merge in a few minutes. Reply "restore the published versions", and it restores your previous skills and plugin in about ten minutes. After publishing, also say "restore the published versions" if your Amp should drop the change too. To stop the mission at any point, reply "stop the mission"; the agent stops after the current step and reports. Undo does not reverse what other missions did under the new rules in the meantime.

## Words you may not know

- **dev:** the shared branch where finished work lands before any release.
- **Milestone:** a group of work items that merge together and end with a report.
- **Review limit:** the number of review rounds allowed before the agent must decide what to do with an open problem.
- **Fresh review:** a check by a new agent that has not seen the author's work notes.
- **Child thread:** a separate Amp thread that does one big work item and reports back to the mission thread.
- **Helper agent:** a short-lived agent inside the mission thread that does one small work item.
- **Branch:** a separate line of changes that does not affect others until it is merged.
- **Merge:** adding a branch's changes into another branch, here into dev.
- **Mission thread:** the Amp thread where this mission runs and where you reply.
